subject: PolarisX dedicated runway & headroom estimate
messages:
From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
To: anna.lopez@polarisx.ai
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 18 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: PolarisX — Dedicated runway & headroom question

Anna,

Great to meet yesterday — following up on the dedicated sizing question you raised. To build a conservative Dedicated slab recommendation we need a couple of inputs (attached is a template CSV for token distribution):

- Typical model(s) you plan to serve (model size & quantization target; e.g., 70B q4o, 13B q8).
- Per-request token breakdown: prompt vs. expected generation (we included polarisx_token_profile.csv template).
- Spike characteristics: duration and multiplier for burst windows (e.g., 5–10x for 30–90s).
- Required SLOs: p50/p95 latency targets and tail constraints for interactive routes.

High-level ask from our side: if you can share a 7-day token/time sample (CSV) or a short summary (avg tokens/day, peak tokens/sec) we can convert that into tokens/sec peak, map to model throughput numbers, and propose slab counts for A100/H100 pools with a recommended headroom percentage to hit p95 targets.

Quick note on our capacity planning assumptions (so you know where numbers will come from):
- We map tokens/sec -> tokens/sec per GPU measured on our runtime for your target model and sequence length distribution (we use historical median seq lengths when absent).
- We apply a 25–45% safety buffer by default depending on burstiness and SLAs; we call this the operational headroom.
- For latency-sensitive routes we prioritize H100-backed slabs and tighter headroom; for high-volume background generation we suggest quantized A100 slabs to reduce cost.

If you can return the token_profile by EOD tomorrow I’ll have an initial ballpark slab proposal by Thursday.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

From: anna.lopez@polarisx.ai

Date: Wed, 19 Jul 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PolarisX — Dedicated runway & headroom question

Karthik,

Thanks — attached is a week sample and the CSV you sent. Quick summary:
- Average tokens / day (7d): 30,400,000 tokens
- Typical interactive request: 1,100 tokens total (300 prompt / 800 generation)
- Concurrent interactive users during normal hours: 180–220
- Peak event: marketing campaign on 7/11 produced a sustained 12-minute window with a 6x spike on request volume, peaks measured ~2,500 req/min
- Nightly batch: non-interactive summarization jobs run 02:00–04:00 PST, producing ~6M tokens over that window (not latency-sensitive)
- Desired SLO for interactive routes: p95 <= 350ms, p99 <= 700ms

We plan to run a mix of two model families: a quantized 13B for fallback/cheap routes and a 34–70B family for highest-quality chat. We marked preferred model variants in the CSV (col: preferred_model).

-Michael (Finance) asked that any Dedicated recommendation include a straightforward mapping to monthly committed GPUs and an expected per-token cost delta vs Hosted.

Attached: polarisx_token_profile.csv (sample), polarisx_mqp_latency_matrix.pdf (historical latency by route).

Anna Lopez
CTO, PolarisX
anna.lopez@polarisx.ai

From: ben.carter@redwood.com
To: anna.lopez@polarisx.ai
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 20 Jul 2028 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: PolarisX Dedicated sizing — initial proposal (ballpark)

Anna / team,

Thanks for the sample — ran it through our workload mapper this morning. Below is a concise, defensible ballpark to start contract conversations and internal capacity planning. Numbers are intentionally conservative to preserve p95 target under spikes.

Assumptions used (from your CSV + internal measurements):
- Interactive peak observed (7d sample): ~42 requests/sec (derived from peak minute scaled to expected campaign behaviors).
- Avg tokens per interactive request: 1,100 tokens (300 prompt / 800 gen).
- Peak tokens/sec (interactive only) = 42 * 1,100 = 46,200 tokens/sec.
- Nightly batch peak (02:00–04:00): ~6M tokens over 2 hours -> ~833 tokens/sec sustained (non-latency-sensitive).
- Model choice: primary = redwood-llm/34b-q4o for chat; fallback = redwood-llm/13b-q8 for cheaper routes.

Throughput mapping (empirical numbers from our runtime for seq len ~800):
- H100-80GB (perf profile for 34B-q4o): ~9,000 tokens/sec per GPU (single-request optimized path, good KV-cache reuse).
- A100-80GB (perf profile for 34B-q4o quantized): ~5,500 tokens/sec per GPU.
- A100-80GB (13B-q8): ~18,000 tokens/sec per GPU.

Dedicated slab recommendation (target: meet peak interactive + 40% operational headroom for campaign-style bursts):
- Using H100 primary approach (recommended for p95 350ms): need base GPUs = ceil(46,200 / 9,000) = 6 GPUs.
- With 40% headroom: 6 * 1.4 -> 8.4 -> round up to 9 H100 GPUs reserved (this is a single-dedicated slab sizing suggestion).

Cost-conscious hybrid alternative (mix H100 + A100):
- Reserve 6x A100-80GB (for cost savings) and 2x H100 as a hot-standby fallback for latency-sensitive spikes. In this pattern A100s will serve most traffic and H100s will take overflow/canary routes. Operational headroom computed similarly results in 8 GPUs reserved (6 A100 + 2 H100).

Notes on SLO fit:
- H100 slab at 9 GPUs provides p95 headroom comfortably for 350ms across most request shapes because of higher single-GPU throughput and lower context-switch overhead.
- A100-only slab meets average throughput but needs the H100 fallback to sustain p95 under sustained 6x bursts unless you accept degraded p95 during extreme campaigns.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Agree on pilot slab (we suggest 6 H100 for a 30–60 day pilot to validate traffic patterns).
2) If pilot succeeds, convert to 9x H100 reserved or hybrid 6 A100 + 3 H100 depending on cost targets.
3) We will instrument route-level tracing and token-level cost dashboards (linked) so finance can see the expected per-token delta vs Hosted.

I can produce an itemized monthly committed GPU and per-token delta table for Michael — want that attached in the proposal deck?

Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Attachment references: polarisx_mqp_latency_matrix.pdf (used to sanity check p95 targets), polarisx_token_profile.csv

Ben / Karthik,

Appreciate the clear breakdown — this is exactly what Michael needed to start a procurement conversation. A few quick asks before we proceed to pilot PO:

- Can you produce the monthly committed-GPU cost vs hosted per-token delta table (Michael requested line-item visibility)?
- We accept the 6 H100 pilot proposal but would like a 60-day pilot at a reduced pilot-rate (team request).
- We need a short addendum describing how audit logs and request-level data retention will be handled for compliance (we will need this for our SOC review).

If you send the updated cost table and a short compliance addendum I’ll loop procurement and legal and aim to return a signed PO within two weeks.

Thanks,
Anna
